I reviewed `d78dc8e5…6dde346f`. There are no must-fix defects, but one finding changes what a signer sees: the summary can round or abbreviate the limit being granted. I'd fix that before opening the PR.

**How this was run.** I ran a condensed single-reviewer pass over all nine areas and did not spawn the paired validate/refute agents. That means the findings are **not adjudicated and there is no score**. Treat this as a checked draft: I verified each finding against the code by hand. I changed nothing, installed nothing, ran no tests and used no `gh`.

**Scope:** 19 files, +860 −0, 8 commits, all new files under `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/Policies/SpendingLimitFlow/PolicySummary/`. It's purely presentational: nothing in the app uses `PolicySummary` yet.

**Repo profile:** web (Next.js) · TypeScript/React · Jest + RTL · ESLint, tsc and prettier via `verify` · rules taken from the root and `apps/web` AGENTS.md files.

## Findings

| # | Priority | Area | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P2** | bugs / security | `PolicySummary/LimitSummaryRow.tsx:33` | The granted limit is shown rounded or abbreviated |
| 2 | P3 | testing | `PolicySummary/__tests__/LimitSummaryRow.test.tsx:24` | The amount test uses the same formatter as the code, so it can't catch #1 |
| 3 | P3 | bugs (plausible) | `PolicySummary/copy.ts:17-19` | The callout and the spender card can show different names for the same spender |
| 4 | P3 | conventions | `PolicySummary/frequency.ts:1` | Deep import into the spending-limits feature |
| 5 | P3 | DRY | `PolicySummary/constants.ts:14-19`, `PolicySummary/testBuilders.ts:11` | The reset-period minute values are written out a second and third time |
| 6 | P3 | KISS (stale comment) | `PolicySummary/testBuilders.ts:8` | The comment gives a reason that isn't true in this diff |

### 1 · P2 — The granted limit is shown rounded or abbreviated
- **What:** `TokenAmount` gets no `preciseAmount`, so it falls back to `formatAmount` (5 decimal places, and compact notation once the number is longer than 9 characters): `packages/utils/src/utils/formatNumber.ts:47-58`.
- **Example:** a typed `0.123456` ETH shows as **0.12346 ETH**, which is higher than the real limit. A typed `1234.56789` shows as **1.23K ETH**. The exact number only appears in the hover tooltip.
- **Why it matters:** this block exists to tell signers exactly what they are granting. `types.ts:13` says the amount is shown "exactly as typed". The existing review step shows full precision (`src/components/tx-flow/flows/TokenTransfer/SendAmountBlock.tsx:41` passes the token's decimals as the precision).
- **Fix:** pass `preciseAmount` to `TokenAmount`, or pass the token's decimals as the precision the way `SendAmountBlock` does.

### 2 · P3 — The amount test can't catch #1
- The expected value at `LimitSummaryRow.test.tsx:24` is built with `formatVisualAmount`, the same formatter the code uses, and `'1000'` never rounds anyway.
- **Fix:** add a test with more than 5 decimals (e.g. `'0.123456'` ETH) and one large amount, and assert the literal strings you expect.

### 3 · P3 (plausible) — Callout and card can name the spender differently
- **Callout:** `spenderDisplayName` (`copy.ts:18-19`) uses only `spender.name`, trimmed.
- **Card:** `EthHashInfo` prefers the address-book name over the `name` prop (`src/components/common/EthHashInfo/index.tsx:17`).
- **Result:** if `name` is undefined but the address book has an entry, the callout says "0x1234…5678" while the card says "Alice". The comment at `copy.ts:17` ("the same fallback the spender card shows") is then wrong.
- **Why only plausible:** this only happens if the model builder (planned for Phase 2) fills `name` from a different source than the address book.
- **Fix:** have the builder use `useAddressBookItem`, or pass `showName={false}` plus the resolved name so both places use one source.

### 4 · P3 — Deep import into the spending-limits feature
- `frequency.ts:1` imports from `@/features/spending-limits/constants`. `apps/web/AGENTS.md` ("Feature Architecture Import Rules") forbids any deep import.
- `getResetTimeOptions` is already exported from the barrel (`src/features/spending-limits/index.ts:17`), and other code already imports it that way (`src/components/transactions/TxDetails/TxData/SpendingLimits/index.tsx:14`).
- **Fix:** import it from `@/features/spending-limits`.

### 5 · P3 — Reset-period values written out three times
- `CANONICAL_FREQUENCIES` (`constants.ts:14-19`) re-keys `'0' / '1440' / '10080' / '43200'`, which already live in `src/features/spending-limits/constants.ts:3-8`.
- `PRODUCTION_PERIODS` (`testBuilders.ts:11`) repeats them a third time.
- If the options ever change, the summary quietly falls back to the dropdown wording.
- **Fix:** at least derive `PRODUCTION_PERIODS` from `Object.keys(CANONICAL_FREQUENCIES)`.

### 6 · P3 — Stale comment in the test builders
- `testBuilders.ts:8` says the builders "must stay importable from stories", but `PolicySummary.stories.tsx` uses inline fixtures and never imports them.
- **Fix:** delete the comment, or reword it to the real reason.

## Checked, nothing found
- **Security:** no secrets, no injection risks, and no transaction-building code in this diff.
- **Regression:** only new files. The only existing code used is `getResetTimeOptions`, `SafeAccountSummary`, `EthHashInfo`, `Card`, `Alert` and `TokenAmount`, and none of them is changed.
- **Performance:** all lists are small.
- **Architecture:** the new code sits next to its siblings and follows their patterns, including the existing `utils/testBuilders.ts`.

## Not covered
- The findings weren't adjudicated, and there's no score.
- I didn't check that it looks like the Figma frame, or render the Storybook stories.
- I didn't run type-check or lint. `radius="lg"` on `Card` is already the default, which is harmless.

## Worth tidying (optional, no score impact)
- Findings 4 and 6 are one-line fixes.
